definition: A model architecture that encodes two inputs (such as a query and a document) independently into separate embeddings, which can then be compared efficiently.
details: Bi-encoders enable fast large-scale retrieval because document embeddings can be precomputed and indexed, unlike cross-encoders which require joint processing of each pair at query time.
story: Imagine a factory floor where each workstation can glance at every other workstation before doing its part. Think of it this way: A model architecture that encodes two inputs (such as a query and a document) independently into separate embeddings, which can then be compared efficiently. And here is the clever part: Bi-encoders enable fast large-scale retrieval because document embeddings can be precomputed and indexed, unlike cross-encoders which require joint processing of each pair at query time. Structure decides what the model can even express — the blueprint before the bricks. And that shape of the machine — Bi-Encoder — is what makes everything else possible.
